newsitem.title: USA: Stock market comes roaring back at opening.
newsitem.headline: Stock market comes roaring back at opening.

text.p: Stocks jumped at the opening Friday, with the Dow industrials surging nearly 50 points in the first 90 minutes of trading and the Nasdaq index recovering all of its heavy losses from Thursday.
The Dow Jones industrial average was up 43.49 points to 6485.98, or about 0.68 percent, at 10 a.m. EST. About 66 million shares changed hands on the New York Stock Exchange.
On Thursday, the Dow surged on a late buy programme, but did not quite make up its earlier loss of 96 points, and finished off 5.78 at 6,442.49.

The Nasdaq Composite sailed up 13.12, or 1 percent, to 1,293.82, erasing its steep losses Thursday, when it closed off 10.33 at 1,280.70. Tech stocks were slammed on concern about poor holiday sales at computer retailers.

Some stocks that analysts had said suffered undeservedly in Thursday's sell-off recovered, including Dell Computer, which rose $1.50 to $52.75, and Gateway 2000, which gained $1.25 to $52.375. Compaq also jumped $1.25 to $73.625 in early trading on the NYSE.

The U.S. Treasury bond market, which sparked Thursday's sell-off following a stronger-than-expected report from the nation's manufacturers, was steady, with the yield on the benchmark 30-year bond unchanged at 6.74 percent.
